title: 3. 现实态与潜在态（Actual and Virtual）

zh: 3. 现实态与潜在态（Actual and Virtual）

en: In his essay on the déjà vu, Bergson writes: ‘Our actual existence, then, whilst it is unrolled in time, duplicates itself all along with a virtual existence, a mirror-image. Every aspect of our life presents two aspects, it is actual and virtual, perception on the one side and memory on the other. Each moment of life is split up as and when it is posited. Or rather, it consists in this very splitting.’

This is just a laconic note, and is not later developed. It is enough, however, to suggest a thesis of some significance: perception fixes the present as real, complete, resolved in unambiguous given facts; whereas memory limits it within the terms of mere potential, retaining something of its
character. The difference between the two forms with which we grasp hold of our ‘now’ is, therefore, a

: the modality of the possible or the modality of the real, memory of potential or perception of the act. In the déjà vu, both modalities join side-by-side and operate in unison, rather than neutralising each other or alternating. That is, in one and the same event we have the paradoxical coexistence of the real and the possible. This event simultaneously seems actual and potential: but, mind, this is the potential of its own act, of itself
act (and not an act due to result from it); and, conversely, this is the act of its own potential, of itself
potential (and not of some prior potential). Rarely would

we experience a situation in which the virtual and the real fully overlap. The synchronic operation of the two different modalities could provoke a hypnotic effect, dilating and congealing the immediate
zh: 柏格森在论述既视感的文章中写道：“因此，我们的现实存在在时间中展开的同时，始终伴随着自身的潜在复本，犹如镜像。我们生命的每一方面都具有双重面貌：一边是现实态，一边是潜在态；一边是知觉，另一边是记忆。生命的每个时刻一经设定便立即分裂。或者更确切地说，它本身就是这种分裂。”

这只是一条简短的说明，后文没有继续展开，却足以提示一个颇为重要的命题：知觉把当下确定为实在的、完备的、已经落实为明确既定事实的东西；记忆则把它限制在单纯潜能的范围内，保留其潜在性质。我们把握“现在”的这两种形式之间的差别，因而是一种模态差别：可能性模态与实在性模态，对潜能的记忆与对实现的知觉。在既视感中，这两种模态肩并肩地结合并协同运作，而不是相互抵消或轮流出现。也就是说，在同一个事件中，实在与可能悖论式地共存。这个事件同时显得是现实的和潜在的；但请注意，这里的潜能是该事件自身之实现的潜能，是它作为实现时的潜能（而非某种日后才由它产生的实现之潜能）；反过来，这里的实现也是它自身之潜在的实现，是它作为潜在本身的实现（而不是某个先在潜能的实现）。我们很少经历潜在与实在完全重合的情境。两种不同模态的同步运作可能产生一种催眠效果，使眼前的此时此地膨胀并凝固。

en: A thesis of this kind (only in some small part possible to infer from Bergson’s text) suddenly raises quite a jumble of problems. We must ask: why on earth should the possible present itself with the aspect of memory? Even when it concerns the instantaneous present, memory places ‘the mark of the past’ on its representation. And is it not bizarre to claim that the past is the chosen abode of the virtual? Bizarre to claim that precisely the past, that miserable cadaster of

’, constitutes the temporal dimension of the modality of the possible? Are we not, perhaps, more used to projecting the potential, that which does not yet exist, into the future? More used to considering it the object of expectation and prediction, and never as some chest of reminiscences?
zh: 这样的命题（其中只有很小一部分可以从柏格森的文本直接推得）立刻引出一团纷繁的问题。我们必须追问：可能性究竟为什么会以记忆的面貌出现？即便记忆所关涉的是瞬间的当下，它仍然会在自己的表象上盖下“过去的印记”。可是，声称过去是潜在态选定的住所，难道不奇怪吗？恰恰把过去——这份由“既成事实”组成的可怜地籍册——说成可能性模态的时间维度，难道不奇怪吗？我们不是更习惯于把尚不存在的潜能投射到未来吗？不是更习惯于把它当作期待和预测的对象，而从不把它视为装满回忆的箱子吗？

en: To understand in what sense the virtual takes the
of the past, thus becoming the prerogative of memory, it is worth lending our attention to another essay by Bergson,

. This is, apparently, a text unconnected to his comments on ‘false recognition’; indeed, the mnestic faculty is not mentioned even in general terms. And yet it seems sensible – or rather, necessary – to compare them. Bergson refutes the mainstream opinion according to which a) the possible
the real, its substitute in embryo; b) it is something

than the real, since even if it fully resembles it, it lacks the decisive requisite of existence. These are two correlated misunderstandings, which mutually feed one another. On closer view, Bergson says, an event becomes possible only
in the moment in which it is realised.
The virtual is contemporaneous to the actual, arises with and duplicates it. Nevertheless, in duplicating the real, the possible detaches itself into the past, and establishes itself there with a

: ‘As reality is created … its image is reflected behind it into the indefinite past; thus it finds that it has from all time been possible, but it is at this moment that it begins to have been always possible.’
zh: 为了理解潜在态如何采取过去的形式、从而成为记忆的特权领域，我们有必要关注柏格森的另一篇文章《可能与实在》。表面上看，这篇文章与他关于“错误再认”的评论毫无关联；文中甚至没有泛泛提到记忆官能。然而，把这两篇文章加以比较似乎是合理的——不如说是必要的。柏格森驳斥了两种主流看法：第一，可能先于实在存在，是实在尚处胚胎阶段的替身；第二，可能少于实在，因为即使它与实在完全相似，也缺少存在这一决定性条件。这是两个相互关联、彼此助长的误解。柏格森说，仔细看来，一个事件只有在得到实现的那一刻才成为可能。
潜在与现实同时出现，同现实一道发生，并将其复分。然而，可能在复制实在之时又脱离出来，退入过去，并以追溯运动在那里立足：“随着实在被创造出来……它的影像便向后映照进无定的过去；于是，它发现自己自古以来一直是可能的，但它恰恰从这一刻起，才成为‘一向可能的’。”

en: When a certain fact takes place, we not only perceive its reality but also feel the texture of its potential. But the being-possible of the fact, though it concerns the present, appears as having-
-possible: through a systematic

, that is. Precisely because it is retrospectively located in a previous time, in the virtual there is more – not less – than in the actual: ‘the possible is only the real with the addition of an act of mind which throws its image back into the past’.
Bergson does not offer any specification of this ‘act of mind’ in which the modality of the possible is incardinated. However, it seems legitimate to give an unambiguous answer to this question.
is the mechanism that confers a potential (incomplete,
contingent) character on actual reality by throwing it back into the past. To be precise, this mechanism is the
namely, that which ‘is in the past in its form and of the present in its matter’.
This is solely due to the inevitable anachronism, which always establishes the virtual afresh. Bergson writes: ‘the possible is … the mirage of the present in the past’.
Meaning: the possible is the

made into an object of memory, placed under the sign ‘back then’, re-evoked in the very moment in which it is lived. The order of potential comes into alignment with the order of memory, to the point of total identification. The symmetrical errors usually committed with regard to each of the two (believing that memory
perception, believing that the possible
the real) require a single correction. The virtual is simultaneous to the actual
memory is simultaneous to perception.
zh: 当某个事实发生时，我们不仅知觉到它的实在性，也体会到它的潜能形态。然而，这个事实之‘可能’虽然关涉当下，却显现为曾经可能——也就是说，它通过一种系统性的时代错置而显现。正因为潜在态被追溯性地安置在先前的时间里，其中所含的东西才比现实态更多，而不是更少：“可能不过是实在再加上一项心灵行动，这项行动把实在的影像向后投进过去。”
柏格森没有具体说明可能性模态寄居于其中的这项“心灵行动”是什么。不过，对这个问题作出明确回答似乎完全合理：记忆正是那个把现实态向后投进过去，从而赋予它潜在性质（不完备、偶然）的机制。准确说来，这个机制就是对当下的记忆，即那种“在形式上属于过去、在质料上属于现在”的记忆。
其原因仅仅在于那种每次都重新建立潜在态的、不可避免的时代错置。柏格森写道：“可能是……当下在过去中的海市蜃楼。”
意思是：可能就是成为记忆对象的此时此地，就是被置于“那时”标记之下、并在亲历它的同一时刻被重新唤起的此时此地。潜能的秩序与记忆的秩序彼此重合，直至完全等同。人们通常针对二者犯下的对称错误（认为记忆晚于知觉，认为可能先于实在），必须通过同一个修正来纠正。潜在与现实同时发生，因为记忆与知觉同时发生。

en: If we consider

in isolation, we get the impression that Bergson denied the modality of the possible any autonomous value. The potentially existing is nothing but a reverberation of the really existing, its image anachronistically transposed onto the past. As such, he seems to echo the theses of the ancient Megarian philosophers, criticised by Aristotle in

according to whom it was necessary to consider possible only ‘what is or will be’. Yet things change as soon as we connect the theme of the virtual to the theme of memory (and, in particular, to analysis of the déjà vu). We know that memory can boast of a difference ‘in nature, not
degree’ with regard to perception. It is a peculiar, irreducible and non-derivative way of grasping the present. But we also know that the possible, having the
of the past, is structured as a memory (where, conversely, the real is totally at one with perception). As such, there is also a

between the potential and the actual: the two modalities, even though they often share the same experiential content, are separated by an unbridgeable hiatus. Far from being liquidated or debased, potential reaches its very acme precisely when it persists as potential alongside the corresponding act. The difference in its nature precludes any assimilation, instead implying its independence: the possible is not cancelled out by the real, as if it were a temporary interlude, but rather represents another way of being, substantial in itself.
zh: 如果孤立地考察《可能与实在》，我们会觉得柏格森否认了可能性模态具有任何自主价值。潜在存在无非是实在存在的回响，是后者的影像经由时代错置被移植到过去。因此，他似乎重述了古代麦加拉学派哲学家的命题——亚里士多德在《形而上学》中曾批评这一命题

——按照他们的说法，只有“现在存在或将会存在的东西”才应被视为可能。然而，一旦我们把潜在态的主题同记忆的主题（尤其是对既视现象的分析）联系起来，情形便发生改变。我们知道，记忆相对于知觉拥有一种“性质而非程度上的”差别；它是把握当下的一种独特、不可还原且非派生的方式。我们也知道，可能具有过去的形式，其结构如同记忆（反过来，实在则与知觉完全一致）。因此，潜能与实现之间同样存在性质而非程度上的差别：两种模态即使经常分享同一经验内容，彼此之间仍隔着无法跨越的断裂。潜能非但没有被取消或贬低，反而恰恰在它与相应的实现并存、却仍保持潜能状态之时达到顶点。性质上的差别排除了同化，并意味着它的独立性：可能并不因实在出现而像一个临时插曲那样被取消；它代表的是另一种自身具有实质的存在方式。

en: The phenomenon of the déjà vu now acquires greater splendour. It (like the idea of an ‘end of history’, as we shall see) concerns the experience of the possible, or better, its pervasive metastasis. The critical point lies in the transformation of a ‘memory of the present’ into a ‘false recognition’: in the former, the virtual comes to light, and is compared side-by-side with the actual; in the latter, conversely, it is abrogated in the most drastic matter, since it assumes the aspect of something
, of an act that occurred previously. Déjà vu arises when the past-
, applied to the present, is exchanged for a past-
, which the present will repeat with obsessive loyalty – that is to say, when the
is exchanged for a
-past. It is difficult to experience the coexistence of the virtual and the actual, certainly, but it has nothing pathological about it
. The (mnestic
historical) pathology consists, rather, in

the dissimulation of the coexistence that we have now outlined, in veiling or exorcising the difficulty that this entails. ‘False recognition’ protects from the burden of the possible, so to speak, the very thing that ‘the memory of the present’ signals.
zh: 既视现象的意义现在更加清楚了。它所关涉的是对可能性的经验，或者更确切地说，是这种经验广泛扩散；正如我们将会看到的，“历史终结”观念也是如此。关键在于，“对当下的记忆”转化成了“错误再认”：在前者中，潜在态显露出来，与现实态并列比较；在后者中，潜在态反而被以最彻底的方式废除，因为它呈现为某种已经成为实在的东西，呈现为一项先前发生过的实现。当适用于当下的过去形式被误认作一种过去内容，而当下又仿佛必须执拗而忠实地重复这一内容时——也就是说，当可能的当下被误认作实在的过去时——既视感便出现了。诚然，体验潜在态与现实态的共存十分困难，但这种共存本身并无任何病态。记忆和历史的病理，反而在于掩饰刚刚概述的这种共存，在于遮蔽或驱除它所带来的困难。可以说，“错误再认”使人免于承受“对当下的记忆”所提示的可能性重负。

en: Ibid., p. 147.

zh: Bergson, ‘The Possible and the Real’, Key Writings, p. 230：“因此，当人断定可能并不以实在为前提时，他便承认实现给单纯可能增添了某种东西：可能仿佛自古以来就在那里，是一具等待自己时刻到来的幽灵；因而，它似乎通过某种添加、某种血液或生命的输注而变成实在。人们没有看见事情恰好相反：可能包含与它相应的实在，此外还多出某种东西，因为可能是实在一经出现之后同一个把它向后投进时间的条件共同作用的结果。大多数哲学所默许、也合乎人类心灵天性的那种观念——可能通过取得存在而得到实现——因此纯属幻觉。”
en: Bergson, ‘The Possible and the Real’,

, p. 230: ‘Thus in judging that the possible does not presuppose the real, one admits that the realization adds something to the simple possibility: the possible would have been there from all time, a phantom awaiting its hour; it would therefore have become reality by the addition of something, by some transfusion of blood or life. One does not see that the contrary is the case, that the possible implies the corresponding reality with, moreover, something added, since the possible is the combined effect of the reality once it has appeared and of a condition which throws it back in time. The idea imminent in most philosophies and natural to the human mind, of possibles which would be realised by an acquisition of existence, is therefore pure illusion.’
Ibid., p. 229.

zh: 同上。
en: Ibid.
